notes.text: The word "distress" doesn't need to mean persecution or problems. The Greek term "anagke" appears 18 times in the New Testament; it is translated by a form of "distress" 8 times, but translated 15 times by its normal meaning of "necessity." Thus Paul is speaking about an exceptional situation that justifies suspension of normal activities, including marriage. Some interpreters say that because of the "present necessity" (Meaning persecutions or problems in the Church), Paul is recommending that people remain single at this time.
"The present distress" would be translated better as "the present necessity," which is the need for
missionaries. Today, most missionaries who serve also delay marriage to serve the Lord.
